title: The Tongue Cut Sparrow
text:
A kind old man in Japan kept a little sparrow that he loved and fed every day. His wife, however, was mean and greedy. One day, while the old man was out, the sparrow pecked at some rice starch she had made for her laundry. In a rage she seized the bird, cut its tongue with scissors and drove it away.

When the old man came home and heard what had happened, he was heartbroken. He went out to search for his sparrow, calling for it through the hills and bamboo groves. At last he found the sparrows' home deep in a bamboo forest. His sparrow welcomed him joyfully, and the sparrows feasted him and danced for him.

When he rose to leave, they offered him a parting gift: a large basket or a small one. The old man said he was old and the road was long, and chose the small one. At home he opened it and found it full of gold, silk and treasure.

His wife at once set off for the sparrows' house and demanded a gift. Offered the same choice, she seized the large basket. She could not wait to see what it held and opened it on the way home. Out came demons, snakes and monsters, and she fled in terror, or in some versions died of fright.
lesson: Kindness and modesty tend to be repaid, and greed tends to choose its own punishment. Take only what you need, and treat small creatures gently.
people: An old man, his wife, a sparrow
